content.title: Addressing Homelessness in Arvada
content.summary: The City of Arvada is actively addressing homelessness through community collaboration, aiming to make the experience rare, brief, and nonrecurring. With approximately 300 unhoused individuals in the area, the city has implemented a transitional housing program at Suburban Studios, which has successfully housed over 125 people since its launch in January 2025. Additionally, the city is engaging residents in discussions to develop effective policies and support tailored to individual needs, with a focus on long-term solutions.
content.body:
Homelessness is a community issue that will take a community solution. The City of Arvada is committed to collaborating with residents, businesses and partnering agencies to create a strategy that will work for everyone in the community, with a goal of making the experience of homelessness rare, brief and nonrecurring.

---

## Help us make an impact

[![Colorado Gives Foundation](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6492)Donate through Colorado Gives](https://www.coloradogives.org/story/Arvadahomelessnavigation)

[![](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6494)Provide supplies through our Amazon Wish List](https://www.amazon.com/hz/wishlist/ls/LBK0XZ9TTFTB?type=wishlist&ref=cm_wl_list_create&relatedRequestID=1JYVC73Z46Z4W6V0QDCT)

---

## What is homelessness?

According to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), homelessness is when an "individual or family lacks a fixed, regular, and adequate nighttime residence." This includes people living on the streets as well as families and individuals transitioning among different settings, like short-stay motels, doubling-up with friends or family members, sleeping in cars or living in transitional housing or shelters.

### Who is homeless in Arvada?

As of 2025, there were roughly 300 people in Arvada who were unhoused. They are not just statistics. They are parents, families, veterans, seniors, pet owners, neighbors. Get to know some of them and their stories on the [City of Arvada YouTube channel](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5fLaqv2Cb40&list=PLJq_TITOXij0lY61jSUmeVZreekPInnY9).

## What we're doing to help

The 2025 Community Survey conducted by the City of Arvada identified homelessness as a top area of concern for residents. The City is working to take strategic action to support programs and services that are proven to help individuals and families who are at risk of losing housing stay in housing and/or transition from homelessness to permanent housing.

### A transitional opportunity

One of the City's most effective strategies has been the transitional housing program at the Suburban Studios extended-stay hotel. The program provides temporary shelter and case management for Arvadans experiencing homelessness. With individualized help in areas like career coaching, housing navigation, and peer support from others with lived experience, the program has been a cornerstone of the effort to reduce homelessness in Arvada. Since launching in January 2025, Suburban Studios has housed more than 125 people.

### A community solution

In response to rising concerns about homelessness, the City facilitated a series of Community Conversations in 2025, creating space for residents to engage in thoughtful, inclusive dialogue about the challenges of homelessness and potential policy responses.

[Read more about the Community Conversations](https://www.arvadaco.gov/1522/Homelessness-community-conversations)

### A people-focused approach

Our passionate team works hand-in-hand with community partners and across City departments to support and coach neighbors experiencing homelessness on their road to self sufficiency. They focus on individual circumstances and needs, tailoring their approach to find what works for each of their clients.

**Lynette Badasarian, Homelessness Program Manager**  
Lynette came to Arvada from the City of Boulder, where she was Homelessness Program Manager for three years.  At Arvada, Lynette will support the City's team and focus on expanding regional service provider collaborations, supporting cold weather operations, and working to refine and implement the City's long term strategy for reducing homelessness in Arvada.

**Rochelle Brogan, Homelessness Outreach Navigator**  
Rochelle helps connect people experiencing homelessness in Arvada with services and support. Before coming to Arvada, Rochelle worked as a certified peer support specialist, supporting people with severe and persistent mental illness. Rochelle brings her own lived experience with homelessness and mental illness to this outreach work that she is passionate to support. Reach Rochelle at 303-392-1924.

**Hudson Janz, Homelessness Case Manager**  
Hudson is a Colorado native and has fallen in love with Arvada. Hudson has worked in the homeless field since 2020 and is honored to be in Arvada, where he does believe that we can work towards solving homelessness. Reach Hudson at 720-693-6832.

**Alexandra Williams, Homelessness Case Manager**  
As a former small business owner in Arvada, Alex developed a deep appreciation for community connection and local impact. She's passionate about engaging with marginalized populations, helping individuals overcome barriers, build stability, and move toward lasting healing through compassionate, collaborative, and resource-focused support. Reach Alex at 720-693-1742.

Alex and Hudson recently appeared on the City's Inside Arvada podcast to share more about their success and challenges. Listen using the player below or wherever you enjoy podcasts, including [Apple](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/inside-arvadas-homelessness-case-management/id1736238466?i=1000689310574), [Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/episode/17qhxkDm7YILU2H1INflon), [YouTube](https://youtu.be/n-tPTnGfTdc?si=fSER6tRXnpb9Hv9s), and [Buzzsprout](https://www.buzzsprout.com/2320363/episodes/16534678-inside-arvada-s-homelessness-case-management) (with transcript).

---

## Learn more

### Are you or someone you know experiencing homelessness?

A number of resources are available from the City and other community partners. Read more on the [**Get support with homelessness page**](https://www.arvadaco.gov/1484/Get-support-with-homelessness).

### What you can do to help

There are volunteering opportunities, organizations that need donations and other ways to join the effort to address homelessness on the [**Help address homelessness page**](https://www.arvadaco.gov/1485/15715/Help-address-homelessness).

## Stay informed

Stay up to date with progress on the City’s response to homelessness, including opportunities to attend community meetings, provide feedback, and volunteer, by signing up for the [Homelessness Response email list](https://www.arvadaco.gov/list.aspx?ListID=282).

## Report a Concern

Homelessness is not illegal, and people experiencing homelessness are still Arvada residents deserving of respect and dignity. The Arvada Police Department’s Community Outreach Resource Enforcement team provides for public safety and conducts outreach to connect people experiencing homelessness to existing services.

- If somebody is in physical harm, you witness an active fire or a crime in progress, or you are concerned for an individual or family's welfare, please call 911.
- If you want to report an encampment, use [Ask Arvada](https://www.arvadaco.gov/898/Report-a-Problem-or-Ask-a-Question) so that the appropriate resources can be deployed.
